hypothesis: After a radio reconnect the DHCP client parks, clears the old lease, starts a fresh transaction and rejects an old ACK.
conclusion: Both cases passed on the host model. Physical DHCP reconnection is unqualified.
narrative: checks/radio-dhcp-reconnect.c (removed from the repository as a one-off radio composition) ran two cases on one AArch64 image with actual FreeRTOS IP-task and owned socket-service execution. The healthy case checked the processed offline epoch, closed DHCP socket and stopped timer, an event processed while parked, old lease expiry during offline, a fresh transaction that rejected an old ACK, a changed address, and a new UDP exchange followed by CLOSE. The acquisition-timeout case restored the same pre-offline checkpoint and suppressed only the modeled server replies; clients stayed closed and failed address authority could not be restored. Initial DORA was setup for the healthy case and was not repeated by the timeout case. Firmware and both authorized association generations were modeled checkpoints; the check did not repeat WPA2 handshakes or execute board startup, the radio session loop, or board_radio_poll. Wire responses, SDIO hardware and entropy were modeled. The evidence directory holds the exact image, source/tool closure, setup stops and checkpoint-bound results.

hypothesis: The composed AArch64 network model runs DHCP acquisition, renewal, expiry, acquisition failure, fixed IPv4 DNS with cancellation, and renewal without a fresh lease option, with actual stack parsing and callbacks over the SDIO model.
conclusion: The four cases passed on the host model; physical RF, network credentials, entropy, radio operation and physical time accuracy are unqualified.
narrative: checks/radio-network-dhcp-dns.py (removed from the repository; its sntp case also ran the SNTP client) built one AArch64 composition and ran four cases: DHCP acquisition, renewal and expiry; acquisition failure; fixed IPv4 DNS and cancellation; and renewal without a fresh lease option. The fixture required an actual ARP cache entry before DNS and an IP-task cancellation acknowledgement before reusing a DNS slot. Standard string routines required by enabled DNS also passed focused semantics checks. Compiler evidence covered all 92 linked objects and 255 source dependencies. Earlier setup and fixture failures remained preserved beside the final image. One earlier DHCP composition missed a 500-tick DNS deadline after ARP became ready; the final composition passed but does not establish timing robustness. The sntp case ran the SNTP client with the actual socket service, FreeRTOS+TCP and DNS over the SDIO model: the modeled server did not answer the first DNS query, answered ARP for the resolved time-server address, sent a datagram from another port and one for another nonce before each valid reply, and the resulting RTC request named the expected day and second. The emulator has no real network.
